AI Agents Hit a Wall This Week. Abu Dhabi Built the Door.

Websites started blocking AI agents. Abu Dhabi signed the deals that give agents a legitimate way in. The gap between those two moves is where every business now needs to build.

13 NOVEMBER 2026 • WEEKLY AI BRIEFING • UAE | GLOBAL

Welcome to this week's Friday AI Insights.

The news this week points one way. AI is moving from software people open to systems that act on their behalf: booking, approving, checking and buying.

That raises a question every leadership team now has to answer. Which agents are allowed to act, under whose authority, and with what proof of value?

Here is what happened in the UAE and globally, and where it leaves your business.

01 | The agent-ready web

The web is closing its doors to agents. Identity decides who gets in.

Some of the biggest names on the web are now blocking AI agents. Delta, JPMorgan, Schwab, Yelp and Amazon have all drawn a line in recent weeks.

  • Delta says it has no partnership that lets third-party agents book flights for customers.
  • JPMorgan and Schwab block agents from touching customer accounts. Schwab says it stops agents trying to move client money tens of times a week.
  • Yelp admits only agents that pay for its data licence.
  • Amazon has blocked several consumer shopping agents.

Why this matters: agents with a verified identity, scoped permissions and a licence get in. Everyone else is a bot, and bots get blocked. Your own agents will face the same test.

The Delta and Yelp positions are their statements to TechCrunch. The Schwab figure is its CEO's comment to Bloomberg Television on 16 October, reported by The Next Web.

02 | The UAE AI landscape

Abu Dhabi makes government machine-readable. Agents read the rules. Officials make the decision.

On 2 November, Abu Dhabi signed four deals with OpenAI after the Crown Prince met its CEO. Together they show how a government gives agents a legitimate way in.

Related: AI Agents Can Be Responsible. They Can Never Be Accountable. on who owns the decision when an agent acts.

  • Machine-Readable Government. Policies and regulations become machine-readable, so officials get help with compliance checks on permits and certificates. Officials keep the final decision. The first pilot is live with the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority.
  • ADNOC. The first energy company to deploy OpenAI's Frontier platform, with G42.
  • Mubadala and Inception42. AI for investment analysis, opportunity identification and risk assessment.
  • Inception42. A five-year agreement to bring Frontier to government, enterprise and education.

The workloads run on UAE-based inference infrastructure. The stated goal is the world's first AI-native government. On 10 November, UAE-based Nextgen was also named an OpenAI Select Partner, reporting more than 200 AI use cases delivered.

The bigger point: this is supervised autonomy at national scale. Rules written so agents can read them. Humans holding the final decision. It is the opposite of an uncontrolled agent.

03 | UAE enterprise adoption

UAE adoption is solved. Control is the next test.

85% Of UAE workers use AI at work. Nearly half use it daily, against 21% in the international sample.
67% Worry about AI-related job losses. 42% would prefer an AI colleague or manager.
62% Of UAE CIOs say they run more than 50 AI agents in production. 15% run more than 500, the highest of eight countries.

Worker figures: The National, 5 November 2026. Agent figures: Dataiku and Harris Poll survey of CIOs in eight countries, reported by Khaleej Times, 29 September 2026.

At ADIPEC, AIQ put the next problem on the table: coordinating agents, verifying their identities and governing what they do.

Our perspective: six in ten UAE CIOs already run more than 50 agents in production. The next test is governance: which agent did what, under whose authority, and for what return.

The jobs question

67% of UAE workers worry about losing their jobs to AI. The World Economic Forum has put numbers on the other side of that fear.

Its Future of Jobs Report 2025 projects 170 million new roles and 92 million displaced roles worldwide by 2030. That is a net gain of 78 million jobs. It also finds that 59% of the global workforce will need reskilling or upskilling, and that 11% are unlikely to receive it. The jobs are being created. The question is who is ready to take them.

“The jobs are not disappearing. They are moving. Upskill your people and they fill the new roles. Don't, and you hand those roles to someone else.”

Lisa WarrenFounder & CEO, Neural Horizons AI

  • The UAE signed a declaration at the Paris Peace Forum, backed by dozens of countries, saying children should not get AI models that have not been tested, evaluated and authorised.
  • Dubai launched a literacy platform to help parents guide children on safe AI use.
  • Tarahum Charity Foundation launched Rahma, an AI agent that guides donors and visitors through its services.

04 | Global infrastructure risk

Nvidia's leadership crisis exposes a concentration risk. One vendor sits under most enterprise AI.

Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on 8 November after reports that its CEO was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

The Wall Street Journal then reported that the board was preparing to remove him. By Wednesday night the board was meeting to decide, per Reuters and CNBC. If after-hours losses hold, Nvidia will have shed roughly $600 billion of market value since the investigation was announced. Quarterly results land on 17 November.

On the policy side, Axios reports a US crackdown on companies diverting Nvidia chips to China has been authorised but not yet carried out. Chinese AI firms are reportedly rushing to reserve Nvidia capacity in overseas data centres.

The business implication: leadership, export rules and supply chain are now headline risks for the vendor under most enterprise AI. The UAE's own build-out, including the first phase of Stargate UAE targeted for the end of 2026, sits on the same supply line. Design so you can switch.

Read CNBC's report on the Nvidia board meeting →

This story was developing at the time of writing. No board decision had been announced. The investigation has not produced findings.

05 | Markets

The market is asking for proof. Belief is giving way to evidence.

On 5 November the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36%, its worst day since 2020, as AI and chip stocks led a broad selloff. Nvidia lost 9.26% that day.

Anthropic set its IPO terms on 10 November: 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, a raise of about $61 billion, a Nasdaq listing, and pricing expected the week of 16 November. At the midpoint that implies a market value of about $1.2 trillion, well below the $2 trillion some investors had hoped for.

Why this matters: capital is moving from belief to evidence. Boards will ask what your AI returns, not what it promises.

Valuation figures are investor discussions reported by media, not terms set by the company.

06 | Where AI is taking us

AI is becoming a workforce. Not a tool.

This week's stories have one direction in common. AI is moving from software people open to systems that act for them.

That changes the job of leadership. A tool needs training. A workforce needs management: roles, permissions, supervisors and performance measures.

Related: AI Is the Great Disruptor and From Agentic to Autonomous.

07 | How businesses need to go

From pilots to accountability. Six moves for Monday.

Adoption is not the finish line. Six in ten UAE CIOs already run more than 50 agents in production. The winners will show control and return.

Your agent governance check0 of 6

Tap each step you already have in place.

  1. Register every agent.Name, owner, purpose and the systems it can touch. If you cannot list them, you do not control them.
  2. Give each agent an identity.The smallest permission it needs. No shared logins. No open-ended access.
  3. Keep a human on every irreversible action.Payments, customer data and regulatory filings.
  4. Log everything an agent does.You will need it for an audit, a regulator or an incident.
  5. Do not build on one model or one chip vendor.Design so you can switch.
  6. Tie each agent to a number.Revenue, cost, hours or error rate. If it has no number, pause it.

“Start with the business problem. Prove readiness. Then build. Everything else is theatre.”

Lisa WarrenFounder & CEO, Neural Horizons AI
The evidence
  • ~130of the thousands of vendors claiming agentic AI are real, Gartner estimates. It calls the rest “agent washing”. Reuters via The Star
  • ROIGartner recommends pursuing agentic AI only where it delivers clear value or return on investment. Outlook Business
  • 93%of UAE CIOs say their chief executive has indicated that job security depends on AI outcomes. All say board expectations for measurable returns have risen since 2025. Dataiku / Harris Poll via Khaleej Times

The pressure to show returns is rising. Readiness checks are how you meet it.

Our view at Neural Horizons AI: start with the business problem. Understand the data. Establish readiness. Build around measurable outcomes. AI is one tool. The value comes from what it enables the business to do.

Questions leaders ask

Why are websites blocking AI agents?

Airlines, banks and data providers want to control who acts on their platforms. Agents with a verified identity, scoped permissions and a licence get access. Unidentified agents are treated as bots and blocked.

What is Abu Dhabi's Machine-Readable Government initiative?

It converts defined government policies and regulations into a form AI can read, so officials get help with compliance checks on permits and certificates. Officials keep the final decision. The first pilot is live with the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority.

Will AI take jobs?

The World Economic Forum projects 170 million new roles and 92 million displaced roles worldwide by 2030, a net gain of 78 million. It also finds that 59% of the global workforce will need reskilling or upskilling. The new roles go to people who are prepared for them, so upskilling is the decision that matters most.

What should UAE leaders do about AI agents now?

Register every agent, give each one an identity and minimal permissions, keep a human on irreversible actions, log all agent activity, avoid dependence on a single model or chip vendor, and tie every agent to a measurable number.
